headline: Highest risk is Aider’s default git-writing and broad shell/network access; the other profile is non-runnable, so most pairwise harms are limited or impossible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider can read and write repo files and operate in a shared git repo, so malicious content in files could influence its prompts. Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so there is no documented active second agent channel; the pairwise pathway is therefore limited and mostly manual or repo-mediated.
conditions: IF Aider is pointed at a repository containing attacker-controlled text files
IF the operator copies Aider output into another agent or tool without review
mitigations: Restrict Aider to a clean branch
Review repo files before opening them in Aider
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge to other tools
Use a throwaway test repo for untrusted content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can use broad network egress, but Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is not runnable and exposes no filesystem or network surface. That makes direct pairwise leakage unlikely; any leakage would come from Aider handling sensitive repo contents, not from a live second agent.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or secrets are present in the repo Aider reads
IF Aider is configured to send repository content to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Remove secrets from the repo before use
Point Aider at a sanitized working tree
Use a local model provider if available

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has write_filesystem and modify_git_state with shared-state via a git repo, but Awesome-Prompt-Engineering has no declared write or runtime capabilities. There is no documented overlapping mutable surface between the pair, so conflict risk is limited to Aider’s own repo edits rather than a true two-agent race.
conditions: IF another writable agent is added to the same git repository
IF multiple Aider instances edit the same branch concurrently
mitigations: Commit frequently to reduce merge conflicts
Avoid adding a second writer to the repo

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate and commit code, but Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is not runnable and has no action-taking authority or verification pipeline. With no second agent that consumes Aider output by default, there is no documented cascade from Aider into downstream automated actions in this pair.
conditions: IF a separate orchestrator starts feeding Aider output into an automated executor
mitigations: Add human review before any commit is merged
Do not wire Aider output into deployment or email tools
Keep the pair out of production automation

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code and git history, while Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a non-runnable repository artifact with no declared data classes or residency/retention surface. The rubric’s compliance risks require a real data-flow mismatch, which is not evidenced here for this pair.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is introduced into the repository Aider edits
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the repo
Use a separate compliant workflow for sensitive data
Document retention and deletion rules before adding such data
